Step 1:

#### Run Setup ####
    chmod +x setup.sh 
    ./setup

#### Verify IAM role attachment ####
    aws sts get-caller-identity


Step 2:

#### Change Directory ####
    cd ~/AIOpsAgent

#### Project Generation ####
    agentcore create

Step 3:

#### Move into the automatically generated directory using ####
    cd ~/AIOpsAgent/myAIOpsAgent

#### Open and adjust your regional environment targets map using ####
    nano agentcore/aws-targets.json 

#### Open the agent definition file located in the application directory ####
	nano app/myAIOpsAgent/harness.json


Step 4:

#### Clear any local build database artifacts to ensure a clean sync run using ####
	rm -rf .cli/rm -rf cdk.out/rm -f agentcore/.agentcore

#### Execute the native deployment command directly from the project directory using ####
	agentcore deploy


Step 5:

#### Test Agent ####

Code Interpreter — shows sandboxed Python execution:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Generate a Fibonacci sequence up to 100 and plot it as a bar chart"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Calculate the standard deviation of [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]"


Browser — shows web automation:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Go to https://aws.amazon.com and tell me the main headline on the page"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Search for the current AWS re:Invent date on the web and summarize what you find"

Scenario A — Real-Time Weather Retrieval (Browser)
    agentcore invoke --prompt "What is the current weather in Seattle, WA? Include temperature, conditions, and wind speed."

    What to observe: The agent autonomously launches the browser, navigates to a live weather source, extracts the relevant data, and returns a structured response — no API key, no SDK.

Scenario B — Operational Data Analysis (Code Interpreter)
    agentcore invoke --prompt "I have server response times in milliseconds: [120, 340, 89, 560, 210, 430, 95, 780, 150, 320]. Calculate the mean, median, p95, and flag any values above 500ms as incidents."

    What to observe: The agent writes and executes Python live, returns computed statistics, and identifies incidents — no local Python environment needed.

Scenario C — Multi-Step Ops Dispatch (Both Tools)
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Check the current weather in Chicago. Then write a Python script that takes the temperature in Fahrenheit and converts it to Celsius, and calculates whether our field crews need cold-weather gear (below 5°C threshold). Output a dispatch recommendation."

    What to observe: The agent:
    Uses Browser to fetch live weather data
    Uses Code Interpreter to run the conversion and threshold logic
    Synthesizes both results into an actionable ops recommendation

Scenario D — Observe the Agent Loop
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Check the current weather in New York and calculate the heat index if humidity is 65%." --verbose

    What to observe:
    The --verbose flag exposes the full agent reasoning trace — which tool was selected, what input was passed, and what the tool returned, making the orchestration transparent.

Step 6:

#### Remove All Resources ####

agentcore remove all
